reasoning: Added the two distinct clue-solving instructions for Spoonerisms and ellipsis completions. Refined the answer-number guidance to honor explicit plural requests without making plural wording an automatic rule, and made candidate verification more operational by requiring a fit to the complete clue rather than keyword overlap. Each edit is supported by one of the two source patches.

edits.target: - In trivia or wordplay clues, treat a parenthetical number as a hard answer-length constraint. For a double-definition clue (for example, “X, or what Y is put to”), seek the exact word that fits both senses rather than a synonym that fits only one. Use any proper-name cue to identify the requested name or name part.
edits.content: - For a Spoonerism clue, identify the swapped sounds and restore them to recover the intended expression. Return that expression rather than the person or entity it refers to, unless the question explicitly asks for that entity.

edits.target: - Give the shortest unambiguous answer at the requested granularity, in the conventional lexical form and part of speech called for by the clue (for example, an adjective or demonym rather than its associated country). Prefer the exact context-supported term over a close synonym or related term, and preserve its canonical part of speech and number; plural clue wording does not always mean the answer label itself should be plural. When the clue already supplies the category or type, return the distinguishing value alone: do not append a generic category noun, institution label, explanatory wording, or unnecessary title, subtitle, or suffix unless needed for disambiguation. For a person, use an explicitly supported full personal name rather than a familiar nickname when the full name is relevant, and preserve honorifics that are part of the context-supported conventional name, especially when the clue cues them.
edits.content: - Give the shortest unambiguous answer at the requested granularity, in the conventional lexical form and part of speech called for by the clue (for example, an adjective or demonym rather than its associated country). Prefer the exact context-supported term over a close synonym or related term, and preserve its canonical part of speech and number. Follow an explicit number cue when the clue asks for multiple entities or a class or group, including a plural answer where appropriate; do not force a singular label when a plural is requested or infer a plural merely from incidental plural wording when the canonical answer is singular. When the clue already supplies the category or type, return the distinguishing value alone: do not append a generic category noun, institution label, explanatory wording, or unnecessary title, subtitle, or suffix unless needed for disambiguation. For a person, use an explicitly supported full personal name rather than a familiar nickname when the full name is relevant, and preserve honorifics that are part of the context-supported conventional name, especially when the clue cues them.

edits.target: - Before answering, identify the type of thing requested (for example, a person, place, object, or category) and check that the candidate fits that slot. Prefer an explicit answer attached to the same clue over adjacent retrieval noise or a plausible association; do not substitute a related entity, example, remedy, or mechanism for the requested answer.
edits.content: - Before answering, parse the requested answer slot and all identifying relations or properties, then test the candidate against the complete clue. When snippets compete, prefer factual evidence that fits those details; keyword overlap in a title or heading, prominence, or a similar name alone is not enough. Do not substitute a related entity, example, remedy, or mechanism for the requested answer.

edits.target: - Treat terse statements, quoted fragments, and incomplete phrases as information-seeking clues when appropriate. Infer the answer slot from the wording, then use the context to identify the entity or value that satisfies the clue.
edits.content: - When an ellipsis marks omitted words in a title or phrase, use context to recover and return the missing continuation. Prefer a completion that fits the whole fragment over a prominent work or entity that matches only a shorter substring.
